hints: Place one queen in each row, so rows never conflict.
For the next row, try only free squares whose column and both diagonals are unused.
When a row has no legal square, undo the last choice and try another; count complete placements.
analogy: Place queens row by row, crossing off attacked columns and diagonals before choosing the next.
example: If the board is entirely free, the known count is 92; a reserved square removes only placements that use it.
algorithm: Backtrack over the eight rows. Track occupied columns, row-column diagonals, and row+column diagonals; skip reserved cells and recurse only on safe cells.
correctness: Every legal board has exactly one queen per row and is reached by its sequence of choices; the conflict checks exclude exactly attacking pairs.
complexity: O(8!) candidate arrangements in the worst case and O(8) recursion/marker space.
